response.title: What can I use to stay cool in my apartment during a summer blackout when gas generators aren't allowed?
response.answer:
If gas generators aren't allowed in your apartment, you still have several good options for staying cool during a summer blackout.

The most practical solution is usually a portable battery power station paired with an efficient fan. If you need actual air conditioning, you'll need a much larger battery system.

Best options for apartment blackout cooling
Shop

1. Portable power station + fan

Best overall

Approx. $300–$1,000+

A rechargeable battery station can run fans, charge phones, and power small electronics without combustion or exhaust. A 1,000 Wh station can run a 30 W fan for roughly 25–30 hours after losses.

Shop

2. Rechargeable fans

Approx. $25–$100

USB-C or battery-operated fans are inexpensive, quiet, and efficient. They don't lower room temperature, but airflow helps your body shed heat. Some can run all night on a charge.

Shop

3. Battery-powered portable air conditioner

Approx. $900–$2,000+

Provides real refrigeration-based cooling, unlike fans or evaporative coolers. Battery runtime is often only a few hours, depending on settings and battery capacity. Hot exhaust must be vented outdoors.

Shop

4. Evaporative cooler

Approx. $60–$250

Uses much less electricity than air conditioning and can cool incoming air in very dry climates. It's much less effective in humid conditions and needs ventilation to avoid moisture buildup.

How long can a battery actually run cooling equipment?

This is the most important consideration before spending money.

Battery runtime calculator

Battery capacity

1,024 Wh

Cooling device
Small USB fan — 10 W
Efficient room fan — 30 W
Evaporative cooler — 100 W
Small portable AC — 500 W
Larger portable AC — 900 W

Estimated continuous runtime

29.0 hours
Assumes 85% usable energy, including conversion losses. Actual results vary.

Notice how dramatically runtime drops when switching from a fan to air conditioning. Running an AC overnight may require several kilowatt-hours of stored energy.

A couple of real battery options

Anker SOLIX C1000X Portable Power Station 1056Wh | 1800W

1,056 Wh capacity · 1,800 W AC output

$599.99

Suitable for extended fan operation and electronics.

BLUETTI AC70P Portable Power Station – 864Wh LiFePO4, 1,000W

864 Wh capacity · 1,000 W output

$429.00

Another compact option for fans and essential devices.

Before buying, check your building's rules for lithium battery storage, charging, and balcony use. Battery stations produce no exhaust, but they still need safe placement and ventilation.

What else helps without electricity?

Close sun-facing blinds during the day, open windows when outdoor air becomes cooler than indoor air, use damp towels or cool showers, and keep drinking water. These measures can make a meaningful difference. 
GovDelivery
+1

Important: Fans alone are not adequate protection during extreme heat, particularly when indoor temperatures reach the mid-90s °F or higher. If your apartment becomes dangerously hot, go to an air-conditioned cooling center, library, or other safe location. 
US EPA
+1

One question that changes my recommendation

Are you trying to actually lower the temperature inside your apartment, or is having a fan blowing on you enough?

If you want real air conditioning during an outage, I can help size a battery-and-AC setup that works in an apartment without a gas generator.
